Architecture for visitors

Engine Overview

Abyssal Engine combines an editor shell, WebGPU renderer, project system, asset registry, and modular gameplay framework.

Project Model

A project is the editor's workspace and the future home for all durable content.

Project
  Mesh Assets
  Material Assets
  Fragment Assets
  future Scenes
  future Recipes

Abyssal uses friendly names in the editor while keeping stable internal identifiers for asset references. This makes content easier to edit without sacrificing reliable links between assets.

MeshAsset

Geometry metadata. Meshes may come from the built-in base mesh library or imported OBJ geometry.

MaterialAsset

Appearance data for ReflectionLit materials, including base color, roughness, metallic, opacity, and emissive settings.

FragmentAsset

An authored assembly made from mesh nodes, empty pivots, transforms, and optional material references.

Construct

A runtime gameplay identity. A Construct can be assembled from Fragments and configured with gameplay data.

Component

Reusable behavior. Movement, targeting, economy, camera, and other behaviors are composed through Components and services.

Renderer

A WebGPU-first renderer using the ReflectionLit path for mesh rendering, plus specialized editor paths for grid, gizmos, and picking.

Wings Assembler Workflow

Base Mesh or imported Mesh
  -> Add to assembly
  -> Build hierarchy
  -> Position, rotate, and scale parts
  -> Assign Materials
  -> Save Fragment into project

Wings Assembler is the embedded workspace for building reusable physical modules. It uses the same editor shell as the world view, but operates inside an isolated preview scene.

Guiding Philosophy

  • Build games, not demos.
  • Morninghollow is the proving ground.
  • Documentation is part of the architecture.
  • Modularity must solve real production problems.

Technology Stack

  • TypeScript for engine and editor code.
  • WebGPU and WGSL for rendering.
  • gl-matrix for vector and matrix math.
  • Vite for local development and static builds.

Tool Philosophy

Abyssal Engine was not created to replace Unreal, Unity, Godot, or Blender. It was created to build the worlds of Keyless Abyss. Blender remains an important future bridge for broad content workflows.
